title: ‘याम्बुनेर’ कथामा अनुभूतिको संरचना {The Structure of Experience in the Story 'yambuner'}
nepali: प्रस्तुत आलेखमा बिना थिङद्वारा रचित याम्बुनेर (२०७७) कथाको समाजशास्त्रीय अध्ययन गरिएको छ । समाजशास्त्रीय अध्ययनका विभिन्न आयाम मध्ये रेमन्ड विलियम्सद्वारा प्रस्तावित अनुभूतिको संरचनालाई विश्लेषणको आधार बनाइएको छ । यो अध्ययन याम्बुनेर कथामा के कस्ता पिँढीआएका छन् र ती पिँढीहरूले प्रभुत्वशाली पिँढीका परिप्रेक्षमा के कस्तो दबाब र तनावको अनुभूति गरेका छन् भन्ने समस्यामा आधारित छ । यही समस्यामा केन्द्रित रहेर ‘याम्बुनेर’ कथाको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनका निम्ति सामग्रीको सङ्कलन पुस्तकालय विधिबाट गरिएको छ भने ती प्राप्तसामग्रीको विश्लेषण गरी निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । अध्ययनका अन्त्यमा प्रभूत्वशाली पिँढीका रूपमा रहेको शासकीय सत्ता र त्यसको दबाबमा दोस्रो पिँढीले गरेको विशिष्ट अनुभूतिलाई देखाइएको छ । प्रभूत्वशाली पिँढीले काँठका तामाङ समुदायमाथि गरेको दमन र शोषणबाट त्यो समुदायका मानिसले दबाब र तनावजन्य अनुभूति गरेका छन् । यसमा उदीयमान पिँढीका रूपमा सोममाया आएकी छ । उसले दबाबजन्य अनुभूतिबाट विद्रोहको जन्म दिएकी छ । यहाँ पिँढी र समुदायबीचको दबाब र तनावको समाधान स्वरूप वैकल्पिक संस्कृतिको निर्माण नभएपनि त्यसको सुरुवातको छनक भने सोममायाका कार्यबाट देख्न सकिन्छ । यसर्थ यसमा उदीयमान पिँढीले नयाँ संस्कृतिको निर्माण गर्ने प्रयास गरेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । राजधानीको नजिक रहेर पनि सँधै सत्ताभन्दा टाढा रहेको अनुभूति गर्नेकाँठका तामाङ समुदायको जीवनानुभूतिलार्ई यस कथामा निकै कलात्मक र मार्मिक ढङ्गले प्रस्तुत गर्नसक्नु लेखकको वैशिष्ठ्य हो र यो नै यसको प्राप्ति पनि हो । {In the presented article, a sociological study of Yambuner (2077) story written by Bina Thing has been done. The story of 'Yambuner' has been analyzed focusing on this problem.  In the presented article, a sociological study of Yambuner (2077) story written by Bina Thing has been done. Among the different dimensions of sociological studies, the structure of cognition proposed by Raymond Williams has been made the basis of analysis. This study is based on the problem of what kind of generations have come in the Yambuner story and what kind of pressure and stress have those generations felt from the perspective of the dominant generation. The story of 'Yambuner' has been analyzed focusing on this problem. Although there is no creation of an alternative culture as a solution to the pressure and tension between generations and communities, the beginning of it can be seen from the work of Sommayaka. Therefore, it has been concluded that the emerging generation is trying to build a new culture. american_english: In the present article, a sociological study of the story "Yambuner" (2077 BS), authored by Bina Thing, has been conducted. Among the various dimensions of sociological study, the structure of feeling proposed by Raymond Williams has been made the basis of analysis. This study is based on the problem of what kinds of generations appear in the story "Yambuner" and what kind of pressure and tension those generations have experienced in relation to the dominant generation. Focusing on this very problem, the story "Yambuner" has been analyzed. For this study, the collection of material was carried out through the library method, and conclusions were drawn by analyzing that collected material. At the conclusion of the study, the ruling authority functioning as the dominant generation and the distinct feeling experienced by the second generation under its pressure have been shown. From the oppression and exploitation inflicted by the dominant generation upon the Tamang community of Kanth, the people of that community have experienced feelings arising from pressure and tension. In this, Sommaya appears as the emerging generation. Out of her experience of pressure, she has given birth to rebellion. Here, although an alternative culture has not been constructed as a resolution to the pressure and tension between the generation and the community, an inkling of its beginning can indeed be seen in Sommaya's actions. Therefore, it is concluded that in this work the emerging generation has made an attempt to construct a new culture. Being able to present the lived experience of the Tamang community of Kanth—who feel continually far from power despite being close to the capital—in a highly artistic and poignant manner in this story is the author's distinctive hallmark, and this is also its achievement.
